title: Enterprise Ask Staging — Rapid Convergence Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and CS are routing high-touch enterprise feature asks into a long backlog with inconsistent scoping and no standard economic/complexity signal. That causes slow SLAs for triage, repeated clarifying questions, and missed opportunities for bundling work across accounts.

Goal: Create a lightweight staging playbook and tooling pattern that aggregates incoming enterprise asks, applies an automated priority-fit score, suggests bundles, and outputs a one-page initial scope + cost proxy within 48 hours for >80% of requests. The deliverable is a combination of a CS intake template, an automated scoring heuristic, an instruction set for PM/Eng reviewers, and a small connector to surface results in the ticket queue.
acceptance_criteria: CS intake form populated with canonical fields (account tier, value hypothesis, required SLAs, data concerns, compliance) and published to internal Sales playbook
Automated scoring runs against new tickets and assigns a 'Fit' tier (A/B/C) with explanations for each input
Playbook produces a one-page initial scoping artifact (summary, rough complexity: low/med/high, rough cost proxy, recommended next-step) for 80% of inbound enterprise asks within 48 hours
PM reviewers can accept/adjust automated bundling suggestions and route to existing work or create a scoped epic
Dashboard shows time-to-first-scope, distribution of Fit tiers, and manual override rate
Hand-off checklist for Dedicated/Private signals added to case routing rules to avoid downstream rework
proposed_flow_steps: 1) Sales/CS submit request via standardized enterprise intake form (required fields: account ARR band, use-case, blocker, security/regulatory flags, desired timeframe)
2) Intake connector normalizes fields and runs scoring heuristic (account weight + impact + implementation complexity estimate + risk flags)
3) System proposes bundling candidates (same customer, same vertical, similar implementation pattern) and generates an initial scope draft
4) Assigned PM reviews draft, resolves clarifying questions with CS (if needed), and tags request with: fit-tier, complexity, recommended next-step
5) Triage routing: Fit A -> Engage solutions engineering and prioritization review; Fit B -> Queue for discovery sprint; Fit C -> Standard backlog / future consideration
6) Metrics update: mark ticket with outcome and populate intake dashboard for weekly review
scoring_heuristic: Inputs: account_tier (0-3), estimated_revenue_impact (0-5), compliance_risk (0-3), engineering_surface_area (0-4), number_of_accounts_requesting (0-4)
Score = account_tier*2 + estimated_revenue_impact*3 - compliance_risk*2 - engineering_surface_area + number_of_accounts_requesting*2
Output mapping: Score >= 18 => Fit A; 12-17 => Fit B; <12 => Fit C

Notes: Heuristic calibrated with sample of 120 past enterprise asks (see Confluence link). We'll iterate thresholds after 4 weeks of live data to reduce false positives/negatives. Edge cases flagged for manual review when compliance_risk >= 2 or engineering_surface_area >= 3
tradeoffs: Speed vs accuracy: Automated scoring accelerates first-pass but will misclassify nuanced security/regulatory asks until thresholds are tuned
Manual labor vs automation: Initial rollout requires PMs to validate automated outputs (higher initial human cost), but reduces per-ticket time once calibrated
Bundling aggressiveness: Larger bundles reduce implementation overhead but increase coordination complexity across accounts and SLAs
Visibility vs noise: More telemetry improves model tuning but can overwhelm the intake dashboard if not filtered by fit-tier and account band
